title: The Hut Is Too Big Now

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder)

collection.description: An elder is left alone in a hut built for many people: fill it with something, or invite a friend to dinner.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Everyone who used to live in (subject)'s hut has, one by one, moved into huts of their own. They visit. They wave. They are all doing well. And (subject) is alone in a hut built for many people, with far too many sleeping mats, far too many pegs, and a cooking pot big enough to bathe a child in.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) decides that if the hut is going to be big, it may as well be useful. (subject.He/she) starts drying flowers in one corner, and keeping seeds in another, and before long the hut smells wonderful and the neighbors are dropping by to ask for seeds. It's still too big. It's also, (subject) admits, rather nice.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) makes far too much stew in the big pot and invites (friend) over to help eat it. (friend) brings someone else. That person brings someone else. By the end of the evening the hut is noisy and warm and there is no stew left. Everyone goes home eventually, and the quiet afterwards feels quite different.
